title.narrative: Strengthening Nutrition and WASH lean season response through inclusive response approach for community Resilience in Borno and Adamawa state.

description.narrative: ltpgtAs published by OCHA in 2025, the humanitarian crisis in NE Nigeria’s BAY States persists, with the armed conflict in its fifteenth year. Attacks on civilians and essential infrastructure have made people more vulnerable and continue to impede access to life-saving assistance. More than 2 million people remain internally displaced, unable to return to their homes due to ongoing insecurity. Protection needs are high, particularly for women and girls who face risks of violence, abduction, rape, and other forms of gender-based violence. Children, especially those unaccompanied or separated from their families, are vulnerable to forced recruitment. Conflict and insecurity have cut people off from their agricultural production, resulting in food insecurity. Climate change is also compounding humanitarian needs at an alarming rate. At least 7.8 million people will need humanitarian assistance in 2025, and the humanitarian community aims to reach 3.6 million of the most vulnerable.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtIn response to the worsening humanitarian situation, ltbgtFRAD, in consortium with Nkafamiya Rescue Mission (NRM) and Elela Care Humanitarian Development Organization (ECM)lt/bgt will implement this project Through Targetedltbgt Nutrition and WASH intervention in Gwoza, Kaga, Bama LGAs of Borno State and Madagali In Adamawa statelt/bgt. With primary focus in hard -to reach areas, the project will reach ltbgt28,000 (F15,960 , M 12,040 ) direct beneficiaries and 112,000 indirect beneficiaries,lt/bgt and the project aims is ltspangtto address the critical and interlinked challenges of acute malnutrition and WASH affecting vulnerable populations. According to the March 2025 Cadre Harmonisé, an estimated 4.6 million people in Nigeria are projected to experience Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels of food insecurity during the peak lean season from June to September. The persistent effects of conflict, displacement, and insecurity continue to undermine agricultural livelihoods, restrict access to farmland, and erode the coping capacities of affected communities. UNICEF estimates that 2.6 million children under five will suffer from acute malnutrition in 2025, with a staggering 1 million expected to require urgent treatment for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) a doubling of cases from 2024. Contributing factors include conflict-induced displacement, limited access to nutrition services, extreme weather conditions, soaring food prices, and significant cuts to life-saving humanitarian funding.
